subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Oxidation is best defined in terms of oxidation number as:
questions.explain: Oxidation corresponds to a loss of electrons and therefore an increase in oxidation number.

questions.q: For the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) → 2NH3(g), the sign of ΔS is:
options: Negative, gas moles decrease from 4 to 2
questions.explain: Moles of gas fall from 4 to 2, so disorder decreases and ΔS is negative.

questions.q: In the reaction Zn + Cu²⁺ → Zn²⁺ + Cu, the reducing agent is:
questions.explain: Zn loses electrons (is oxidised) and reduces Cu²⁺, so Zn is the reducing agent.

questions.q: For two half-cells, which species is the stronger oxidising agent?
options: The one with the more negative E°
The one with E° closest to zero
The one with the more positive E°
The one with the larger concentration
questions.explain: A more positive E° means a greater tendency to be reduced, so that species is the stronger oxidising agent.

questions.q: What is the oxidation number of manganese in the permanganate ion, MnO₄⁻?
questions.explain: With O at −2 (×4 = −8) and overall charge −1, Mn must be +7.

questions.q: Given E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V, the EMF of the standard cell is:
questions.explain: E°cell = E°(positive electrode) − E°(negative electrode) = +0.34 − (−0.76) = +1.10 V.

questions.q: What are the products when calcium reacts with cold water?
questions.explain: Ca + 2H2O gives Ca(OH)2 + H2; Group 2 metals form the hydroxide and hydrogen gas with water.

questions.q: Given ΔHf[CO2] = −394 and ΔHf[H2O] = −286 kJ mol⁻¹, and ΔHc[CH4] = −890 kJ mol⁻¹, calculate ΔHf[CH4] (combustion gives CO2 + 2H2O).
What is the oxidation number of chromium in the dichromate ion, Cr₂O₇²⁻?
questions.explain: 7 O at −2 give −14; with overall −2, the two Cr total +12, so each Cr is +6.

questions.q: Which statement about changing concentrations in a half-cell is correct (qualitatively, via Le Chatelier)?
options: Concentration changes never affect electrode potential
Only temperature affects electrode potential, never concentration
Increasing the concentration of the species being reduced makes its electrode potential more positive
Increasing reactant concentration always makes E°cell negative
questions.explain: Raising the concentration of the oxidised species shifts the half-cell equilibrium, making that electrode potential more positive.

questions.q: Using ΔHc (combustion data), the enthalpy of a reaction is calculated as:
questions.explain: With combustion data the cycle gives ΔHr = ΣΔHc(reactants) − ΣΔHc(products).

questions.q: For an exothermic reaction, which is true of the reaction profile?
options: Products are higher in energy than reactants
Products are lower in energy than reactants and ΔH is negative
questions.explain: Exothermic reactions release energy so products lie below reactants and ΔH < 0.

questions.q: How does the solubility of the Group 2 sulfates change down the group?
options: Solubility decreases down the group, with BaSO4 essentially insoluble
questions.explain: Group 2 sulfate solubility decreases down the group; BaSO4 is essentially insoluble, which is why barium sulfate is used in the test for sulfate ions.

questions.q: A reaction has ΔH = +50 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS = +100 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. The temperature at which it becomes feasible is:
questions.explain: At ΔG=0, T = ΔH/ΔS = 50000/100 = 500 K (above this it is feasible).

questions.q: Which is the correctly balanced half-equation for the oxidation of Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺?
questions.explain: Losing one electron raises iron from +2 to +3, so Fe²⁺ → Fe³⁺ + e⁻.

questions.q: In a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell operating in alkaline conditions, the overall reaction is:
questions.explain: A hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen to produce only water.

questions.q: How does the solubility of the Group 2 hydroxides change down the group?
options: All Group 2 hydroxides are equally insoluble
Solubility is greatest for magnesium hydroxide
questions.explain: Group 2 hydroxide solubility increases down the group, so Mg(OH)2 is least soluble and Ba(OH)2 most soluble.

questions.q: Given E°(Cl₂/Cl⁻) = +1.36 V and E°(Br₂/Br⁻) = +1.07 V, which is correct?
options: Br₂ can oxidise Cl⁻ to Cl₂
Cl₂ can oxidise Br⁻ to Br₂
questions.explain: Cl₂ has the more positive E°, so it acts as the oxidising agent and oxidises Br⁻ to Br₂.

questions.q: An oxidising agent is a species that:
options: donates electrons and is itself oxidised
accepts electrons and is itself reduced
questions.explain: An oxidising agent oxidises another species by accepting its electrons, so the agent is reduced.

questions.q: A reaction with ΔH > 0 and ΔS < 0 is:
questions.explain: With ΔH positive and ΔS negative, ΔG is always positive, so it is never feasible.

questions.q: When chlorine is added to cold dilute sodium hydroxide, what type of reaction occurs and what are the products?
options: Disproportionation, giving NaCl, NaClO and water
questions.explain: Cl2 + 2NaOH gives NaCl + NaClO + H2O; chlorine is simultaneously oxidised (to +1 in ClO-) and reduced (to -1 in Cl-), so it disproportionates.

questions.q: A reaction with ΔH < 0 and ΔS > 0 is:
questions.explain: With ΔH negative and ΔS positive, ΔG is negative at all temperatures.

questions.q: Burning 0.0050 mol of a fuel raises 100 g of water by 20.0 °C (c = 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹). What is the enthalpy of combustion?
The Gibbs free energy change is given by:
questions.explain: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS.

questions.q: The first electron affinity of a non-metal is usually:
questions.explain: Adding the first electron to a neutral gaseous atom releases energy, so it is exothermic.

questions.q: Why is the second electron affinity of oxygen endothermic?
options: Oxygen has a full outer shell
The nucleus attracts the electron strongly
Energy is needed to add an electron to an already negative O⁻ ion against repulsion
questions.explain: Adding an electron to a negative O⁻ requires overcoming repulsion, so it is endothermic.

questions.q: In the test for halide ions, which precipitate colour confirms a bromide ion when silver nitrate solution is added?
questions.explain: AgBr forms a cream precipitate, between the white of AgCl and the yellow of AgI.

questions.q: Even when a reaction has ΔG < 0, it may not proceed at a measurable rate because:
options: The activation energy is high (kinetic, not thermodynamic, limitation)
questions.explain: Feasibility is thermodynamic; a high activation energy can still make the rate negligibly slow.

questions.q: When magnesium burns in oxygen, what is the product and the nature of its oxide?
questions.explain: Magnesium burns to form magnesium oxide, MgO, which is a basic (metal) oxide.

questions.q: The standard hydrogen electrode is assigned a standard electrode potential of:
questions.explain: By definition the SHE is the reference with E° = 0.00 V.
